validated_work_order.understanding: PR #15 (commit 97938bb) left three pieces of its own scaffolding behind. (1) Balance.tsx:102-103 still parses a preview row id by hand (`id.slice(8).split('/')[0]`) while all five sibling call sites read it through parsePreviewId; for every id the producer makes the two forms agree, so it is consistency, not a behaviour fix. (2) upcoming-release-notes/ carries two Bugfixes notes crediting Shivam-Fl for one change — post-scheduled-transaction-on-its-own-date.md describes the advance-the-schedule mechanism #15 deleted, fix-schedule-occurrence-consumption.md describes what shipped. (3) The same commit flattened setNextDate's `if (dateCond) {...}` into a `dateCond ? ... : null` ternary, renamed the local nextDate to currentNextDate to accommodate an explicit parameter a later commit in the same PR removed, and reworded the comment above it. The two forms are semantically identical, so ~25 lines of the schedule write path carry pure re-indentation and a name no reviewer would pick. Nothing a user sees changes.
validated_work_order.root_cause: PR #15 was force-pushed over mid-review: the earlier revision advanced next_date via an advanceScheduleToDate helper and gave setNextDate an explicit nextDate parameter, and the surviving revision replaced both with per-occurrence consumption. The final squash kept the three edits the intermediate revisions needed — Balance.tsx's inline id parse, the second release note, and the setNextDate re-indentation, rename and comment rewording — none of which the shipped design needed.
validated_work_order.approach: Four mechanical edits, no new behaviour. (1) Balance.tsx: widen the shared/transactions import to { isPreviewId, parsePreviewId } and replace the two inline lines with `const { scheduleId } = parsePreviewId(id);`, dropping the preview-format comment now documented on the helper. The date field is deliberately unused: SelectedBalance sums schedule._amount, identical across occurrences of one schedule, and each occurrence already has its own row in selectedItems. (2) Delete post-scheduled-transaction-on-its-own-date.md and carry its still-true clauses into the survivor's single body line. (3) app.ts: revert the setNextDate hunk to commit 9065a36's text verbatim, restoring `// Only do this if a date condition exists`, `if (dateCond) { ... }` and the nextDate local. The reference image is the immutable SHA 9065a36, NOT HEAD~1: HEAD~1 is a ref that moves once this change is committed, and at QA time it would resolve to 97938bb — the revision being reverted — so the comparison would report a false difference. `97938bb^` is equivalent and equally immutable, since the file is byte-identical between 9065a36 and 9e554ca. (4) Nothing else: no signature change, no new parameter, no test edits.

validated_work_order.debate_summary: The previous plan (v1) was rejected on a single point, and it was right: it anchored its central no-behaviour-change argument — a diff of the whole reverted function — to `git show HEAD~1:...`, and asserted four times that HEAD~1 was commit 9065a36 and that 9065a36 was the parent of 97938bb. Both halves are false. `git rev-parse 97938bb^` is 9e554ca, not 9065a36. HEAD~1 is also a ref that moves: once the implementer commits, HEAD is the new commit and HEAD~1 resolves to 97938bb, the revision being reverted, so the step the plan called "the authoritative comparison" would have reported a difference on a correct implementation. The error survived v1's own check only because the two candidate revisions happen to hold byte-identical copies of app.ts. v2 replaces every occurrence of HEAD~1 with the immutable SHA 9065a36 in files[3].change and qa_script step 4, drops the false ancestry claim, and states the direct check instead (`git rev-parse 97938bb^` is 9e554ca; the diff between 9065a36 and 9e554ca is empty). The v1 justification `git log --oneline -- <path>` is removed: it lists commits that touched a file, not their positions in history, so it never established ancestry. Re-reading the code for this revision turned up one thing v1 missed: 97938bb also reworded the comment above the block from '// Only do this if a date condition exists' to '// Only derive one if a date condition exists'. Since the QA check is a whole-function byte comparison against 9065a36, that comment reversion is now named explicitly in files[3].change and in the reject-reasons for the partial-revert alternative. Everything else in v1 was re-verified against the working tree rather than carried over: the single slice(8) at Balance.tsx:103, both duplicate release notes with identical category and author, the eight schedule tests, the four call sites passing no nextDate, and the release-notes script's validateFile rules. Two small factual corrections went in alongside: AC-2 no longer asserts the docs generator 'runs clean' without qualification — it exits ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on an uninstalled checkout because it imports '@actual-app/ci-actions', so it is now qualified as requiring `yarn install` — and the delete rationale quotes the actual body text of the leftover note.
residual_risks: An implementer who reaches for HEAD~1 or main instead of 9065a36, following the ticket's literal `git show main:...`, will diff the function against itself and conclude there is nothing to revert — or will produce a comparison that fails at QA for the wrong reason. files[3].change and qa_script step 4 both name the SHA and explain why the moving ref is wrong, but the ticket itself still says main.

The reworded comment ('// Only derive one if a date condition exists') is an edit v1 never named. If the implementer reverts only the rename and the ternary but leaves the comment, the whole-function byte-diff in qa_script step 4 reports a one-line difference on an otherwise correct revert.
